setbackRulesFact.note: Codified from City of Waco Code of Ordinances Chapter 28 (Zoning), Article IV (District Regulations), Divisions 2-6, cross-verified against the City of Waco Planning & Zoning Department's official published summary table 'Chart 1. Yard setback requirements' at https://www.waco-texas.com/files/sharedassets/public/v/2/departments/planning-amp-zoning/documents/chart1yardsetbackrequirements.pdf (accessed 2026-09-06). Primary ordinance text for individual sections was read via the eLaws mirror of the Code of Ordinances at waco-tx.elaws.us (accessed 2026-09-06) because library.municode.com, the canonical live host, returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; eLaws' section text matches the Chart 1 PDF numerics exactly everywhere both were checked, so the two are treated as independently corroborating. WebSearch-surfaced text (not independently confirmed by direct fetch of the primary page) put the live Municode Code of Ordinances as 'codified through Ordinance No. 2025-778, enacted October 21, 2025'; that overall currency date is reported as-is but is NOT independently verified against a directly-fetched primary page, and no section-specific amendment date is available for Divisions 2-6 of Article IV or for section 28-904. SHIPPED rows: R-E, R-1A, R-1B, R-1C, R-2 (the five 'R' district classes covering estate, single-family, and two-family/attached-single-family use, matching in scope the single-family-and-adjacent breadth covered by the Austin (SF-1/2/3 + MF) and Pflugerville (SF-S/SF-R + MF/2-F) tables). Each row's front/side/rear values are the 'All dwellings' (or equivalent standard-use) scalar row from Code section §28-276 (R-E), §28-301 (R-1A), §28-326 (R-1B), §28-351 (R-1C), §28-376 (R-2); each district's ordinance text also carries a materially different 'Other' (non-dwelling) use row and, for R-1C/R-2, a separate single-family-attached/zero-lot-line row with a 10-foot COMBINED side yard in place of the two-yard scalar - both are OMITTED from this table because the schema carries one scalar side_ft per district and the dwelling-use row is the dominant/default case. R-1B and R-1C also each carry a distinct 'special permit uses' row (R-1B: 25/6/25; R-1C: same as its base 'all dwellings' row) that is likewise omitted as a secondary case. side_corner_ft for all five rows is sourced from Code §28-904(f) (Article V, Division 2, 'Yards and required open space'), which sets a 15-foot minimum side-street yard on corner lots in 'the R and O districts' generally; Chart 1 only fills in an explicit numeric side-corner value for the R-E row (15, matching §28-904(f) exactly) and leaves the column blank for R-1A/R-1B/R-1C/R-2, so this table applies the same general-provision value to those rows rather than treating the blank cell as zero or unspecified. §28-904(f) is NOT a flat 15-foot rule: it also provides that a lot of record under 75 feet wide need only provide 20 percent of lot width as the corner side yard, and that where a corner lot's rear yard abuts an adjacent lot's side yard, the corner side yard must instead equal that adjacent lot's required front-yard depth (whichever is greater) - both exceptions are disclosed in the per-field quote below rather than folded into the scalar. max_height_ft (35 for all five rows) is drawn from Code §28-275/28-300/28-325/28-350/28-375, each of which caps height at '2 1/2 stories or 35 feet,' whichever is more restrictive; the 2.5-story component is not separately representable in this schema and is disclosed per-field. max_lot_coverage_pct and max_impervious_pct use the established non-binding sentinel 100 (per the Pflugerville precedent in this same corpus) because Chapter 28 Article IV Divisions 2-6 (Purpose/Permitted uses/Special uses/Lot area/Height/Yard/Additional regulations/Distance requirement sections) and Chart 1/Chart 2 contain no lot-coverage-percentage or impervious-cover-percentage scalar for these districts; a general Waco-wide search for such a figure returned nothing applicable to R-E/R-1A/R-1B/R-1C/R-2. OMITTED: R-3A-R-3E (multi-family), O-1/O-2/O-3, C-1-C-5, M-1-M-3, PUD, Brazos River Corridor, College and University Neighborhoods, Neighborhood Conservation, Airport Overlay, West End, Downtown, and Historic District overlays (Article X) - none were in scope for the single-family/two-family residential envelope this table serves, and none were checked. Yard setback requirements' at https://www.waco-texas.com/files/sharedassets/public/v/2/departments/planning-amp-zoning/documents/chart1yardsetbackrequirements.pdf (accessed 2026-09-06). Primary ordinance text for individual sections was read via the eLaws mirror of the Code of Ordinances at waco-tx.elaws.us (accessed 2026-09-06) because library.municode.com, the canonical live host, returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; eLaws' section text matches the Chart 1 PDF numerics exactly everywhere both were checked, so the two are treated as independently corroborating. WebSearch-surfaced text (not independently confirmed by direct fetch of the primary page) put the live Municode Code of Ordinances as 'codified through Ordinance No. 2025-778, enacted October 21, 2025'; that overall currency date is reported as-is but is NOT independently verified against a directly-fetched primary page, and no section-specific amendment date is available for Divisions 2-6 of Article IV or for section 28-904. setbackRulesFact.note: Codified from the City of Leander Code of Ordinances, Chapter 14 (Zoning), Exhibit A Zoning Ordinance, Article VI (Site Standards) Section 6 (Setbacks) — Supplement 4 Update 1, codified through Ordinance No. 25-078-00 enacted December 18, 2025 (Municode ProductID 12187, job Id 487773). Source is Municode; the setback values cite Article VI Sec. 6, the single-family building/structure setback table. MODELING NOTES: (1) The Leander setback table columns are Front, Side, Street Side, Rear. 'Street Side' is codified as side_corner_ft (the corner/street-facing side). (2) The Leander zoning ordinance (a form-based/SmartCode-style code) states NO simple per-district maximum building height in feet and NO per-district lot-coverage or impervious-cover cap in the dimensional/setback or lot-size-summary sections; max_height_ft, max_lot_coverage_pct, and max_impervious_pct are therefore all not_specified and carry 100 as non-binding stand-ins (the envelope draw uses setbacks, not these fields). (3) SFC/SFL side is stated "5' or 0' & 10'" (attached / zero-lot-line option); the conventional 5 ft interior side is codified and flagged. SFT side is stated "0 or 10'" (attached / detached option); the attached 0 is codified as the base with the alternative flagged. (4) Districts with a note-marked garage/ROW exception (front value carries '*', min 18' to ROW for the garage) retain the table's stated front building setback. (5) Nonresidential/multifamily districts (NR/MF/LO/LC/GC/HC/HI) use a Max-Front + Min-Front + Min-Side + Street-Side + Min-Rear format; the Min values are codified where present, Max-Front is not a setback minimum and is excluded. LO and LC share a table row; codified identically.

setbackRulesFact.note: RECONCILED 2026-09-07 (CTX-B dispatch, operator-ruled) between this repo's prior 4-district Article-II-single-family-only table and legacy-design-tools' independently-researched 10-district table, both derived from City of Round Rock Zoning and Development Code, Code of Ordinances Part III (2018 Edition), Chapter 2, Article II (Residential Districts), Section 2-26 (Residential Lot and Building Dimensional Standards), retrieved via https://roundrock-tx.elaws.us/code/coor_ptiii_ch2_artii_sec2-26 (Round Rock's own library.municode.com pages return HTTP 403 to automated fetch; no field here reaches human-verified against a real code-section atom -- round_rock_tx has 361 real atoms and Sections 1-50/2-26 both exist as real ingested atoms, but neither atom's bodyText captures the dimensional-standards chart's actual cell values, a table-extraction gap, not a corpus absence -- so every field here is primary-source-verified). RULING 1 (side_corner_ft, ALL 10 districts): this repo's DERIVATION wins over the other table's assumption. Chapter 1 definitions, Section 1-50 ('Front Lot Line'), state 'In cases where two or more lot lines abut an existing or dedicated street, all such lot lines are considered front lot lines for the purposes of calculating building setbacks' -- a general Chapter 1 rule, not limited to Article II's single-family rows -- so side_corner_ft = front_ft on every district Article II tabulates no separate corner figure for. The other table instead mirrored the base side setback (an unmotivated assumption, and the permissive/smaller-setback direction for a buildable envelope) on all 10 districts; that reasoning is superseded here. One district, TH (Townhouse, Single-lot), is the exception: Section 2-26's own row tabulates an explicit adjacent-to-street side value ('5 ft./20 ft.' interior/adjacent-to-street) rather than leaving a blank cell for Section 1-50 to fill, so TH's side_corner_ft is that directly-tabulated 20 ft, not a Section-1-50 derivation off its 15 ft front_ft (the other table's own provenance quote already named this 20 ft value but the table's stored side_corner_ft field left it at 5, mirroring side_ft instead -- a bug, corrected here, not a re-derivation). RULING 1 AMENDMENT (2026-09-07, second review): MF-2 was flagged, then resolved. Applying the derivation there would produce 15 ft, LOOSER than the superseded side-mirror convention's 25 ft (MF-2 is the only district where front_ft < side_ft, so the derivation loosens instead of tightens). A derivation is trustworthy when it tightens a figure (safe if the underlying legal reasoning turns out imprecise) and is NOT sufficient on its own when it loosens one (unsafe if wrong) -- so MF-2's side_corner_ft is REFUSED rather than derived: no primary-source citation was found for a distinct MF-2 corner value, and 25 ft (the more conservative candidate) is carried as a not_specified placeholder pending one. Every other district's derivation was checked against this same tighten/loosen test and tightens (or, for SR, is unchanged): none of the other 9 needed this exception. RULING 2 (district breadth): all 10 districts (SF-R, SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, MH, TF, TH, SR, MF-1, MF-2) are carried, not just the 4 this file previously shipped -- six districts do not fall to absence. RULING 3 (SF-3 side_ft/rear_ft): REFUSED, not picked. The two source tables read different, genuinely different sub-columns of the same Section 2-26 SF-3 chart cell -- this file's prior research read the zero-lot-line option (side_ft=12, rear_ft=15), the other table read the Standard-Lot sub-column (side_ft=5, rear_ft=10) -- and a parcel's GIS zoningCode of 'SF-3' cannot distinguish which sub-type actually applies on the ground. Both are defensible, differently-reasoned readings of the same table cell, not an error on either side. side_ft and rear_ft below carry the zero-lot-line reading (12/15, the larger, more conservative pair) ONLY as a required-by-schema numeric placeholder, flagged not_specified: true with an explicit refusal quote -- a correct reader must treat SF-3's side_ft/rear_ft as unresolved pending a real per-parcel sub-type read, not as a settled value. RULING 4 (max_height_ft sentinel): unified to 999 (this file's prior value) across all districts, not 100 (the other table's prior value) -- both were flagged not_specified: true, but 999 cannot be mistaken for a real building height in feet the way 100 (a physically plausible height for some multifamily district) can, and this repo's gate.ts enforces the 999 sentinel by rule G7 whenever not_specified is set on max_height_ft, so the invariant is checked in code, not left to a convention. front_ft/rear_ft/side_ft/max_lot_coverage_pct/max_impervious_pct for SF-R/SF-1/SF-2 and MH/TF/TH/SR/MF-1/MF-2 (the non-SF-3 rows) are unchanged from whichever source table alone: SF-R/SF-1/SF-2 core dimensional cells were the two source tables' one point of full agreement; MH/TF/TH/SR/MF-1/MF-2 were carried from legacy-design-tools' table (this file did not previously ship them).

setbackRulesFact.note: City of Martindale, Caldwell County, TX. INSTRUMENT: Code of Ordinances Chapter 155 (Zoning), Sec. 155.075 - Sec. 155.084, "Property development standards" per district. The chapter's own ordinance-history parentheticals name Ord. 08-347 (passed 2008) for the district standards, with Sec. 155.076 (R-1), Sec. 155.077 (R-1A), Sec. 155.079 (R-3), Sec. 155.080 (R-4) and Sec. 155.082 (C-1) additionally amended by Ord. 2013-08-06 (passed 8-6-2013) and Ord. 2013-08-20-1 (passed 8-20-2013); effectiveDate is that latest recorded amendment, 2013-08-20, NOT a code-currency date. ROUTE AND THE WALL, STATED PLAINLY: the authoritative host for this code is American Legal Publishing (codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/martindale/latest/martindale_tx). It is NOT reachable from this lane: a plain fetch with a Chrome UA returns HTTP 403 with the Cloudflare interstitial ("Performing security verification ... Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue", issued 2026-09-16), and a sub-request to the chapter TOC route 0-0-0-1629 returned the same 403. The text coded here was instead read from the CITY'S OWN official zoning page, https://www.martindale.texas.gov/2211/Zoning, fetched live 2026-09-16, which reproduces Sec. 155.076 - Sec. 155.084 verbatim with their section numbers and their (Ord. ...) history lines, and which the city publishes with the notice "This website is intended for general information purposes only. Please review Sec. 155 Zoning Code of the City's Code of Ordinances for complete zoning regulations." A CURRENCY RISK REMAINS AND IS NOT HIDDEN: because the code host is walled to this lane, the chapter's "current through" revision date could not be read at source, so a post-2013 amendment to these district standards cannot be ruled out. Field values are coded at confidence 0.85 rather than the 0.9 used where the host itself was readable. MODELING. (1) The ordinance regulates IMPERVIOUS COVER, not building footprint coverage: every district's Sec. 155.08x(C)(7) reads "Maximum impervious cover for all uses in the ... District shall be ...% of the lot area." Those figures are coded under max_impervious_pct as real values, and max_lot_coverage_pct is not_specified for every district because the chapter states no separate building-coverage cap. (2) "Street side setback" is the corner-lot / side-street standard, coded under side_corner_ft; the interior side yard is coded under side_ft. Several districts state the street-side standard as ten feet "unless the side street is a major thoroughfare, in which case the minimum street side setback shall be 20 feet" -- ten feet is the general case coded, and the thoroughfare condition is preserved in the quote. (3) R-2's street-side sentence contains a drafting cross-reference error in the source: it reads "The minimum street side setback for all uses in the R-1A district" inside Sec. 155.078 (R-2). The R-2 value is coded (ten feet, thoroughfare 20 feet, identical to R-1A's) and the error is preserved verbatim in the quote rather than silently corrected. (4) MU (Sec. 155.081) is coded with every dimensional field not_specified on purpose: the district states "Because the MU Mixed Use District encompasses the downtown core of the city, limited district-based property development standards shall apply" and requires new or in-fill development to "conform to the setbacks, height and massing of existing structures found throughout the Mixed Use District" -- a per-parcel context standard, not a scalar, so no number is asserted and the district should be treated as a refusal rather than a served row. (5) I (Sec. 155.084, Industrial) states no height standard at all -- its development-standards list runs lot size, front, rear, interior side, street side, lot coverage, landscaping -- so max_height_ft is not_specified and carries the gate's canonical 999 sentinel (rule G7). SENTINELS: not_specified carries 100 for the yard/coverage fields and 999 for max_height_ft, per the corpus gate's G7 rule. No value in this table is a converted or interpolated number; 28.5 feet is the ordinance's own figure (it is the 2-1/2-story height it states alongside). COVERAGE BASIS: the P-255 census's no-table city rows carry no per-district stamp breakdown for Martindale, so the row set is the ordinance's own district list (Sec. 155.075 - Sec. 155.084): R-1, R-1A, R-2, R-3, R-4, MU, C-1, C-2, I -- nine rows, one per district. The live GIS stamp vocabulary could not be re-read in this lane (no staged layer for this city).

setbackRulesFact.note: Codified from City of Waco Code of Ordinances Chapter 28 (Zoning), Article IV (District Regulations), Divisions 2-6, cross-verified against the City of Waco Planning & Zoning Department's official published summary table 'Chart 1. Yard setback requirements' at https://www.waco-texas.com/files/sharedassets/public/v/2/departments/planning-amp-zoning/documents/chart1yardsetbackrequirements.pdf (accessed 2026-09-06). Primary ordinance text for individual sections was read via the eLaws mirror of the Code of Ordinances at waco-tx.elaws.us (accessed 2026-09-06) because library.municode.com, the canonical live host, returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; eLaws' section text matches the Chart 1 PDF numerics exactly everywhere both were checked, so the two are treated as independently corroborating. WebSearch-surfaced text (not independently confirmed by direct fetch of the primary page) put the live Municode Code of Ordinances as 'codified through Ordinance No. 2025-778, enacted October 21, 2025'; that overall currency date is reported as-is but is NOT independently verified against a directly-fetched primary page, and no section-specific amendment date is available for Divisions 2-6 of Article IV or for section 28-904. SHIPPED rows: R-E, R-1A, R-1B, R-1C, R-2 (the five 'R' district classes covering estate, single-family, and two-family/attached-single-family use, matching in scope the single-family-and-adjacent breadth covered by the Austin (SF-1/2/3 + MF) and Pflugerville (SF-S/SF-R + MF/2-F) tables). Each row's front/side/rear values are the 'All dwellings' (or equivalent standard-use) scalar row from Code section §28-276 (R-E), §28-301 (R-1A), §28-326 (R-1B), §28-351 (R-1C), §28-376 (R-2); each district's ordinance text also carries a materially different 'Other' (non-dwelling) use row and, for R-1C/R-2, a separate single-family-attached/zero-lot-line row with a 10-foot COMBINED side yard in place of the two-yard scalar - both are OMITTED from this table because the schema carries one scalar side_ft per district and the dwelling-use row is the dominant/default case. R-1B and R-1C also each carry a distinct 'special permit uses' row (R-1B: 25/6/25; R-1C: same as its base 'all dwellings' row) that is likewise omitted as a secondary case. side_corner_ft for all five rows is sourced from Code §28-904(f) (Article V, Division 2, 'Yards and required open space'), which sets a 15-foot minimum side-street yard on corner lots in 'the R and O districts' generally; Chart 1 only fills in an explicit numeric side-corner value for the R-E row (15, matching §28-904(f) exactly) and leaves the column blank for R-1A/R-1B/R-1C/R-2, so this table applies the same general-provision value to those rows rather than treating the blank cell as zero or unspecified. §28-904(f) is NOT a flat 15-foot rule: it also provides that a lot of record under 75 feet wide need only provide 20 percent of lot width as the corner side yard, and that where a corner lot's rear yard abuts an adjacent lot's side yard, the corner side yard must instead equal that adjacent lot's required front-yard depth (whichever is greater) - both exceptions are disclosed in the per-field quote below rather than folded into the scalar. max_height_ft (35 for all five rows) is drawn from Code §28-275/28-300/28-325/28-350/28-375, each of which caps height at '2 1/2 stories or 35 feet,' whichever is more restrictive; the 2.5-story component is not separately representable in this schema and is disclosed per-field. max_lot_coverage_pct and max_impervious_pct use the established non-binding sentinel 100 (per the Pflugerville precedent in this same corpus) because Chapter 28 Article IV Divisions 2-6 (Purpose/Permitted uses/Special uses/Lot area/Height/Yard/Additional regulations/Distance requirement sections) and Chart 1/Chart 2 contain no lot-coverage-percentage or impervious-cover-percentage scalar for these districts; a general Waco-wide search for such a figure returned nothing applicable to R-E/R-1A/R-1B/R-1C/R-2. OMITTED: R-3A-R-3E (multi-family), O-1/O-2/O-3, C-1-C-5, M-1-M-3, PUD, Brazos River Corridor, College and University Neighborhoods, Neighborhood Conservation, Airport Overlay, West End, Downtown, and Historic District overlays (Article X) - none were in scope for the single-family/two-family residential envelope this table serves, and none were checked. CORRECTION (2026-09-07): all provenance entries originally shipped as verification_state 'human-verified' with a fabricated atom_did (e.g. waco_tx/coor/28-276) that never resolved against any real ingested code-section atom -- no code-section atom corpus exists for waco_tx at all (confirmed directly against the live atoms store). Relabeled to 'primary-source-verified' (a state added in legacy-design-tools PR #628 for exactly this gap) and atom_did removed; the underlying research (real primary-source fetches, cross-verified against two independent sources) is unchanged, only the overclaimed verification status is corrected.
